analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md, head lines 379-381. It adds DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS and rewrites the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE row. No executable code, authentication, attestation, encryption, billing or trust-boundary behavior is modified in the supplied evidence.

The documented behavior concerns scheduler prefill chunk sizing for engine throughput and KV charges. It says the paged pool sizes windowed rings from max(chunk, stripe), so raising the chunk increases KV charges. It also says malformed, zero or negative values restore defaults, and that Gemma 4 bidirectional media blocks keep 512 when the chunk is wider. All of this is local, process-environment configuration, read at process start and forwarded to the LaunchAgent. An operator controls it, which is already inside TB-003 and ADV-001's power. The docs do not claim it grants serving RAM or qualifies a route.

The prefix-cache threat T-041 is unaffected. The docs make no change to cache TTL, HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping or the SSD tier. I did not observe any change to the SEC-035 TTFT oracle. Larger chunk sizes may alter prefill timing, but that is speculative and not shown here.

Limits: the underlying Swift implementation (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift) is not supplied. I cannot confirm that the docs match the code, including the memory admission and KV accounting behavior for values above the default stripe. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the base and head ranges are marked complete. The documentation-only change gives no evidence of a security regression. If the matching code change lands elsewhere, the next pass should check that the KV and memory admission accounts for the wider chunk (a DoS/OOM concern under T-029/T-016-type availability threats) and that the LaunchAgent passthrough allow-list adds only these two variables.
